title: EvidencePackage
description: The bounded set of authorised passages one question is answered from (master plan 12.4, the last step before grounded generation). INTERNAL: it is passed from retrieval to answer generation inside the core and is never serialised to a client, because its items carry source_egress and source_classification. It is bound to the application, tenant, workspace and principal it was authorised for and is never reused for another. It is bounded twice, by item count and by estimated model tokens, so the Lite context budget holds. An empty package is valid and means nothing authorised matched: answer generation turns it into NoSupportedEvidence, never into an uncited answer. Items are in rank order and their handles run e1, e2, ... in that order.

scope.description: The scope and principal the evidence was authorised for, from the verified request context.

query.description: The question the package answers, as the caller asked it.

created_at.description: When the core built the package, from its clock, after the final authorisation and version recheck.

items.description: The evidence, best first. May be empty.

budget.description: The caps the package was built under and what it used.

application_id.description: The application the request was bound to.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the request was bound to.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the request was bound to.

principal_id.description: The principal whose permissions the evidence was checked against.

max_items.description: The most items the package may hold, from the resource budget.

max_toks.description: The most estimated model tokens the items may cost together, from the resource budget.

est_toks.description: The sum of the items' est_toks. Never above max_toks (checked by the core).

truncated.description: True when authorised candidates were dropped to stay inside max_items or max_toks.

methods.description: The pipeline stages that contributed. At least one.

notices.description: Labels for a degraded or adjusted retrieval, for example reduced_semantic_recall. Empty means none.
